questions.question: What is total mercury and how is it different from methylmercury?
questions.answer: Total mercury (tHg) is the sum of all mercury species in a sample, and it is a common measurement in routine food surveillance. The toxicity of dietary mercury is dominated by methylmercury, so total mercury is an analytical quantity rather than a direct measure of the most harmful form. See the [methylmercury](/metals/mercury-methyl) page for the toxicologically primary discussion.

questions.question: Why can't a total mercury number in food be read as the health risk directly?
questions.answer: Because dietary mercury toxicity is driven mainly by methylmercury, interpreting a total mercury result for health usually requires either species-specific measurement (speciation) or the assumption that a matrix-dependent fraction of the total is methylmercury. Elemental mercury vapor, inorganic mercury, and methylmercury need to be interpreted separately even when a dataset reports only total mercury [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]].

questions.question: What are the legal limits for mercury in fish and seafood?
questions.answer: The EU sets binding maximum levels for mercury in fishery products and molluscs: 500 ug/kg for general crustaceans, molluscs, and fish muscle meat, and 300 ug/kg for a listed group of lower-mercury fish [[regulations/eu2023-contaminants-maximum-levels]]. These are the compliance figures for many fish products, though methylmercury remains the primary dietary toxicology concern.

questions.question: Which fish are allowed to have the highest mercury levels under EU rules?
questions.answer: A listed group of higher-mercury fish is permitted up to 1000 ug/kg under the EU maximum levels, including tuna, shark, swordfish, marlin, halibut, pike, and sturgeon [[regulations/eu2023-contaminants-maximum-levels]]. This is higher than the 500 ug/kg general limit and the 300 ug/kg limit for listed lower-mercury fish.

questions.question: Is total mercury or methylmercury the number used for regulatory compliance?
questions.answer: Total mercury is the compliance analyte for many fish rows, meaning it is the measurement of record used to check against limits. Methylmercury, however, is the primary driver of dietary mercury toxicology, so product interpretation still requires methylmercury caution even where total mercury is the enforced measurement.
